title: CPA and TCPA explained: the two radar numbers every OOW must watch

scenes.label: MARITIME TERM OF THE DAY
scenes.heading: Two radar numbers tell you if a target will pass clear.
scenes.narration: Two numbers on your radar tell you whether a target will pass clear, or come dangerously close.

scenes.heading: CPA & TCPA
scenes.body: Closest Point of Approach and Time to Closest Point of Approach
scenes.narration: CPA is the Closest Point of Approach: how near a target will pass if neither vessel changes course or speed. TCPA is the time left until that moment.

scenes.label: ON THE RADAR
scenes.heading: CPA 0.3 nm in 12 minutes
scenes.narration: This target will pass three cables from you in twelve minutes. If your Master's standing orders require one mile, that is too close, and you must act now.

scenes.label: USE IT PROPERLY
scenes.heading: Do not trust it blindly

items.title: Give ARPA time to settle
items.text: After either vessel alters course or speed

items.title: Check speed and heading input
items.text: Wrong input gives a wrong CPA

items.title: Watch the compass bearing
items.text: Steady bearing, closing range: risk of collision

scenes.narration: But do not trust it blindly. ARPA needs time to settle after either vessel alters. Wrong speed or heading input gives a wrong CPA. And always confirm with the compass bearing: if it is steady and the range is closing, risk of collision exists.

scenes.label: KEY TAKEAWAY
scenes.heading: Small CPA, short TCPA: act early.
scenes.narration: Small CPA and short TCPA mean one thing: act early.

meta.description: CPA (Closest Point of Approach) and TCPA (Time to CPA) are the two radar and ARPA values that tell the officer of the watch how close a target will pass and when. What they mean, how to use them, and why the compass bearing still matters.
